text: SUPERSEDED 2026-09-04 -- now a MIGRATION-REMEDIATION TRACKER, not a port plan. The original 'port agent-intercom (Rust) to a feature-complete, CGO-free Go implementation' framing is RETIRED, and the Rust repository at C:\Source\GitHub\intercom (softwaresalt/agent-intercom @ 41df772) is DEMOTED from behavioral oracle to HISTORICAL REFERENCE ONLY (governing decision D8). It is NOT an oracle for operator UI, transport, configuration schema, or credentials, and parity with it is NO LONGER a definition of done -- the two products no longer share an operator surface, a transport, or an agent boundary. VOID: the entire P4-P15 successor ordering recorded in this entry (internal/models + SQLite 7-table schema, the remaining repos + retention, the ACP subprocess risk slice with spawner/handshake/codec/reader/writer, AgentDriver + ACP driver, the Slack Socket Mode slice, the Slack surface with slash commands/modals/9 handlers/US17 thread replies, diff-apply/approval/terminal-gate/policy/audit as scoped there, internal/agenttools with the 9 MCP wire tool names, the resilience slice as scoped, IPC + intercom-ctl, the 56/22/46/6 parity corpus sweep, and the cutover-with-Rust-fallback decision). Slack, ACP, and the parity corpus are all retired; the MCP HTTP tool endpoint retention decision (D1) is likewise void because it existed to serve ACP subprocesses. STILL VALID and carried forward: the shipped foundation 001-F/001-S, error taxonomy + path containment 002-F/002-S, and config package 003-F/003-S (the last now under corrective remediation). WHAT THIS ENTRY NOW TRACKS: residual migration cleanup where retired-architecture surfaces survive in shipped code -- currently the internal/apperr Kind taxonomy contamination (stash 8C2D578D) and any further contamination the U-E1a retired-architecture gate surfaces. The forward roadmap is NOT here: it is phases C1-C11 in docs/plans/2026-09-04-intercom-go-architecture-correction-plan.md, governed by docs/decisions/2026-09-04-intercom-go-architecture-correction-copilot-sdk-deliberation.md. The ORACLE CORRECTION recorded in the original text (references\herdr is ogulcancelik/herdr, a Rust terminal multiplexer, NOT an oracle) remains accurate and is preserved; herdr stays untouched, git-excluded, and non-governing. Priority dropped from high to medium: this is cleanup tracking, not a delivery driver. STAGE DISPOSITION 2026-09-04 (dark-factory cycle post-005-S): RETAINED as a standing tracker. Its sole open item, the internal/apperr Kind taxonomy contamination (stash 8C2D578D), was harvested this cycle into feature 009-F / shipment 008-S. The tracker is NOT archived because its function is continuous: it must catch further retired-architecture contamination surfaced by the U-E1a gate across phases C3-C11, and retiring it the moment its backlog momentarily empties would remove the mechanism exactly when new code starts landing. Adversarial review challenged the open-endedness, so a CONCRETE COMPLETION CONDITION is now attached: archive this tracker when BOTH (a) 009-F has closed AND (b) the U-E1a retired-architecture gate has been broadened back to internal/** (reversing the D6a narrowing) and passes - condition (b) being the real signal that manual contamination tracking is no longer needed. Governing artifact: docs/decisions/2026-09-04-intercom-go-residual-hardening-triage-deliberation.md (decision D-C).

GOVERNING PRODUCT DIRECTION (corrected 2026-09-04; UNBLOCKED). intercom-go is a per-workspace Go backend brokering a GitHub Copilot agent session between two co-equal operator surfaces: a local Bubble Tea TUI and a remote SPA reached over a Microsoft Dev Tunnel. CORRECTIONS APPLIED to this entry's original text: (1) the remote client is an SPA, NOT iOS -- the iOS wording is stale; SPA framework choice is deliberately OUT OF SCOPE; (2) the agent boundary is the OFFICIAL GitHub Copilot SDK for Go (github.com/github/copilot-sdk/go, pinned v1.0.11 = commit a550258d5c37bd662197536992a23d633bfe5804), NOT coder/acp-go-sdk -- intercom-go implements no ACP broker, no ACP wire protocol, and no direct headless-Copilot-CLI lifecycle. That the SDK internally manages a Copilot CLI server over JSON-RPC is an SDK IMPLEMENTATION DETAIL (its codec is under internal/ and unimportable by hosts); (3) the three load-bearing conflicts recorded here are RESOLVED: durability -- the backend projection is a CACHE and the SDK runtime is the durable event source via GetEvents/ResumeSession, bridged by the D4a minimal session pointer (a pointer, not a store; D7 full persistence remains deferred); operator surface in the persistence schema -- moot, Slack is retired so slack_ts/thread_ts/channel_id vanish with it; lifecycle ownership -- settled as one isolated process per workspace, orchestrated by autoharness, one allocated HTTP/WS port (the second ACP port is gone). (4) The AgentDriver-vs-OperatorGateway distinction recorded here is PRESERVED and now realised: the SDK adapter is the agent-facing side, and the OperatorGateway (event envelopes, hydration/reconnect, first-responder arbitration, WebSocket backpressure) is the operator-facing side. GOVERNING ARTIFACTS: docs/decisions/2026-09-04-intercom-go-architecture-correction-copilot-sdk-deliberation.md; docs/design-docs/intercom-go-backend-architecture.md (revision 2); roadmap and next slice in docs/plans/2026-09-04-intercom-go-architecture-correction-plan.md (phases C1-C11). NEXT SLICE: C1 corrective (config remediation + Go 1.24 floor + anti-regression gate), harvested and queued as a shipment. Open operator decisions carried forward: Q1/H2 Copilot CLI version floor (blocks C2); Q3/H3 Dev Tunnel auth (blocks C10); Q6/H4 sessions-per-process (blocks C9); H5 permission authorization model (blocks C5); H6 session-pointer store semantics (blocks C4). NO BLOCKERS REMAIN for C1. STAGE UPDATE 2026-09-04 (C2 harvested): C1 is SHIPPED (004-S, PR #15) -- the 'NEXT SLICE: C1' text above is stale. The next slice is C2 per D9a, now harvested as feature 006-F and QUEUED AS SHIPMENT 005-S. Q1/H2 is NO LONGER A BLOCKER: the 'Q1 blocks C2' annotation above contradicts the governing deliberation, whose Q1 disposition states the spike must RECORD the CLI version it validated against and that this becomes the provisional floor -- Q1 is an OUTPUT of C2, not an input (resolved as decision D10; operator confirm-by-exception). Remaining open decisions are unchanged: Q3/H3 Dev Tunnel auth (C10), Q6/H4 sessions-per-process (C9), H5 permission authorization (C5), H6 session-pointer semantics (C4); NEW Q7 (how intercom reaches workspace tooling) raised by the design-doc reconciliation. ADDITIONAL GOVERNING ARTIFACTS: docs/decisions/2026-09-04-intercom-go-implementation-design-reconciliation-deliberation.md (D10-D14; classifies docs/design-docs/intercom-architecture-implementation-design.md as a CANDIDATE VISION document, NOT governing) and docs/plans/2026-09-04-intercom-go-c2-sdk-spike-plan.md. This entry REMAINS ACTIVE as the standing roadmap tracker for C3-C11. STAGE DISPOSITION 2026-09-04 (dark-factory cycle post-005-S): RETAINED as the standing roadmap tracker for phases C3-C11. Not implementable work; it is the governing product-direction record and the ONLY index of five unresolved operator decisions (Q3/H3 Dev Tunnel auth blocking C10; Q6/H4 sessions-per-process blocking C9; H5 permission authorization blocking C5; H6 session-pointer semantics blocking C4; Q7 workspace tooling reach). Archiving it would destroy that index. C3 (agent adapter / ACL) is the next FEATURE phase but was deliberately NOT harvested this cycle: operator rule 6 makes refactoring for composability/reliability take priority over adding features, and C3 builds directly on internal/apperr and internal/pathsafe, both of which are corrected by shipments 008-S and 009-S. Harvesting C3 first would enlarge its blast radius. Governing artifact: docs/decisions/2026-09-04-intercom-go-residual-hardening-triage-deliberation.md (decision D-C).
